content: Erythromycin and sulfisoxazole are prescribed together to treat specific bacterial ear infections, primarily in children. This medication may also be used for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Erythromycin and sulfisoxazole are available as an oral liquid. It is typically taken every six hours (four times daily) for a duration of 10 days. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than prescribed. Shake the liquid well before each use to ensure the medication is evenly mixed. Drink a full glass of water after each dose. Continue taking the medication even if you feel better. Do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. Before taking erythromycin and sulfisoxazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to erythromycin, sulfisoxazole, azithromycin (Zithromax), clarithromycin (Biaxin), dirithromycin (Dynabac), diabetes medications, diuretics (water pills), or any other drugs. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially other antibiotics, anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), astemizole, carbamazepine, clozapine, cyclosporine, digoxin, disopyramide, ergotamine, felodipine, lovastatin, oral contraceptives, phenytoin, terfenadine, theophylline, triazolam, and vitamins. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had kidney or liver disease, allergies, anemia, asthma, glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G-6-PD) deficiency, jaundice, colitis, or stomach problems. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking erythromycin and sulfisoxazole. Do not take this medication with or immediately after consuming fruit juices, carbonated drinks, or tea. It can be taken with or between meals. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Erythromycin and sulfisoxazole may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: upset stomach, diarrhea, vomiting, stomach cramps, or mild skin rash. If you experience severe side effects, such as a severe skin rash, itching, hives, difficulty breathing or swallowing, wheezing, stomach pain, yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, pale stools, unusual tiredness, sore throat, fever, joint pain, blood in urine, unusual bleeding or bruising, or dark, tarry stools, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it refrigerated and discard any unused medication after 14 days. Do not freeze it. Consult your pharmacist about proper disposal methods for unused medication. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor may order specific lab tests to monitor your response to erythromycin and sulfisoxazole. Do not share this medication with others. Your prescription is likely not refillable. If you still have symptoms of infection after completing the medication, contact your doctor.
